resources.string: Thank you for installing my car logbook application.\n\nPlease read the information section to understand the functionality.

Welcome once again to my application.

This is a completely free product that I, a student and car enthusiast, initially created only for personal use, but decided to share with you as well. I have no goal to make money from this or gain popularity — I just wanted to build a car logbook that is convenient by my own standards.

All data is stored only on your device — the app has no server of its own. To avoid losing your records when reinstalling the app or switching phones, there are two backup options (the section with the floppy-disk icon in the main menu):

1) Local export/import. "Export data" saves a single archive file (database + all photos and documents) to a location of your choice. Later you can "import" this file and your data will be fully restored.

2) Cloud backup to Yandex.Disk. Connect your Yandex account with the button in the same section (a browser opens; the app only gets access to its own CarLog folder on the Disk). After that you can create backups manually, and with auto-backup enabled a copy is created automatically a few minutes after your data changes (when online). The three most recent copies are kept, and you can restore from any of them.

You can contact me through the contacts listed in the app settings — please report any bugs you find and I will try to fix them in updates.

Here you manage your cars. You can:

• Add new cars with photos and detailed information (make, model, VIN, license plate, fuel type, gas equipment, etc.)
• Edit car information
• Delete cars (all related records will also be deleted)

The car card is the entry point to every section: parts, maintenance, accidents, consumables, refuelings, other expenses, documents and statistics.

The current mileage is maintained automatically — it always equals the maximum mileage across all records. You can update it manually with the update-mileage button on the card. If you enter a value below the current one, the app warns you and asks for confirmation: once confirmed, records with a higher mileage are lowered to the new value as well — otherwise the previous maximum would come back automatically.

Section for tracking consumable materials:

• 11 standard categories are always visible: engine oil, transmission oil/fluid, brake and coolant fluids, filters (oil, air, fuel, cabin), front and rear brake pads, battery
• About 30 more optional categories (spark plugs, belts, discs, tires, wiper blades, bulbs, etc.) can be enabled in the section settings
• For each consumable you specify installation date, mileage, manufacturer, part number, cost (volume for fluids)
• Replacement intervals by mileage and/or time; custom values can be set in the section settings
• Traffic-light status on the card: green — all good, yellow — more than half of the resource used, red — replacement is due very soon or overdue
• Replacement history for each category

The best way to replace a consumable is via its details screen (the "Replace" button) or via scheduled maintenance — the old consumable is archived automatically.

Direct adding also works: if the category already has an active consumable, it is archived as replaced.
Oil consumption: the engine oil screen has a "Top up oil" button, and on replacement you are asked how much the level dropped (in ml or by dipstick). Consumption in L/1000 km is calculated per oil and on average. Tracking can be turned off in settings.

Accounting for all parts and assemblies of the car:

• Adding parts with indication of name, manufacturer, part number
• Installation date and current mileage
• Cost of the part and installation work
• Mark about breakdown with indication of date and mileage
• Ability to replace the part (creates a new record, the old one is marked as broken)
• Part photos
• Notes and comments

This allows you to keep a complete history of all installed parts and track their reliability.

A single log of all work done on the car. Each record has one of three types:

• Repair — fixing a breakdown (can be marked as warranty repair)
• Scheduled maintenance — requires at least one replaced consumable; old consumables of the same categories are archived automatically
• Modification — upgrades and improvements

A record includes name, description, date and mileage, parts cost (as a total amount or as a list of specific parts — they will appear in the Parts section), service work cost, service name and address, photos and notes.

Helps track all work on the car and plan the maintenance budget.

Accounting for road traffic accidents:

• Date, mileage and place of the accident
• Damage description and severity (minor / medium / serious / total)
• Your role: at fault or victim (the at-fault party can only receive a KASKO payout)
• Insurance payouts: OSAGO, KASKO, from the culprit
• Repair cost — as a total amount or as a list of parts (they will appear in the Parts section marked "Accident")
• Photos from the scene and one PDF document (e.g. the accident report) — it can be opened from the details screen

Accident expenses appear in statistics as a separate category that can be excluded from calculations.

Accounting for all car refuelings:

• Date, mileage and refueling location
• Fuel volume and type (gasoline grades, diesel, gas with LPG/CNG equipment — CNG in m³; charges in kWh for electric cars)
• Cost per unit or total cost (the other one is calculated automatically)

Average consumption is calculated automatically: all refuelings except the first are divided by the distance driven between them. No need to mark a "full tank". Gasoline grades are counted together, gas and gasoline separately. For a car with gas equipment, enter the distance driven on this fuel in each refueling — otherwise consumption is estimated from the total mileage.

If the tank (cylinder, battery) capacity is set in the car card, the range per tank is shown too.

Missed a refueling? Tap "Restart calculation" next to the average consumption.

Accounting for all other car expenses:

• Categories: self car wash, accessories, car audio, interior detailing, wheels, tires, other
• Date, mileage, name and amount of the expense
• Service information (name, address)
• Notes

Insurance, technical inspection and vehicle tax are tracked separately — in the Documents section.

Allows you to keep a complete record of all car expenses and analyze their structure.

Keep track of your car documents' validity:

• Standard types: OSAGO, KASKO, vehicle tax — their tiles are always visible; plus any custom documents via the "Other" type
• For policies the type and expiry date are required; optional: number, insurer, start date, cost, photo, notes
• For the tax you enter the last assessment date (usually the car registration date) — the app will remind you of the next assessment a year later; the tax has no number or organization fields
• Traffic-light status: green — more than 30 days left, yellow — 30 days or less, red — 7 days or less or expired
• The "Renew" button archives the old document and creates a new one — the History tab shows how the policy price changes year over year
• There is always exactly one active document of each standard type

Document costs appear in statistics as a separate "Insurance and taxes" category.

Detailed car statistics — five tabs:

• General: expense distribution by category, spending trend, cost per km, average km per day and month, the most expensive month
• Fuel: average consumption, volumes and costs by fuel type, charts
• Repairs: amounts and counts, parts vs labor breakdown, distribution by work type
• Other expenses: structure by category, top 5
• Consumables: average maintenance cost, expenses by category

Filters apply to every tab: period (or a specific month), mileage range, exclude accidents. All data is presented with graphs and charts.
Date, mileage and service are taken from the record itself

no need to mark a \"full tank\" anymore: consumption is calculated from all refuelings and shown right in the refueling list, with the same restart button as in statistics. Gas and gasoline are counted separately for cars with gas equipment, CNG is in m³.
set the tank capacity in the car card (battery capacity for an electric car, gas cylinder with gas equipment) and the app will show how far you drive on a full tank.

top up oil with the \"+ Top up\" button right on the oil tile in consumables and note how much the level dropped when replacing it — in ml or by dipstick. The app calculates consumption in L/1000 km per oil and on average, so you can see whether it has grown. Can be turned off in settings.
a new oil or other fluid card takes the volume from the previous replacement; you can still change it.

the \"Fines\" section is now \"Fines, toll roads\": on the second tab, record the date and amount of a trip and, optionally, which road (the app suggests names from your previous entries). Spending is shown by month and as a monthly average; statistics count it as a separate category, not included in the cost per km.

service names (in maintenance, parts and other expenses) and fuel station names you have entered before appear under the field — just tap one. The address of a chosen service is filled in automatically.
if a category would be left without a current consumable, the app offers to put the previous one back.

statistics no longer lose a consumable after \"replace with the same\" or service work for a standalone consumable, and maintenance consumables are no longer counted twice on the chart. Accident payouts and repair costs entered with a space (\"15 000\") are no longer lost on saving.
